steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Common pop progressions: I-V-vi-IV (four-chord loop), I-IV-V (rock/blues), ii-V-I (jazz cadence) — each creates a different harmonic character. | Key Fact: Accompaniment styles define genre: Alberti bass (Classical), riff (rock/pop), broken chords (Romantic), ostinato (minimalist), pedal/drone (folk/traditional). | Key Fact: Harmonic rhythm (how often chords change) affects momentum: fast harmonic rhythm creates drive; slow harmonic rhythm creates stasis and calm. | Key Fact: Dominant seventh chords (V7) create tension that resolves to the tonic — they are essential for cadences and key-defining progressions.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how chords and accompaniment writing are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use chords and accompaniment writing. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use chords and accompaniment writing in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
